question.prompt:
A rectangular grazing area is to be fenced off on three sides using part of a \(100\) meter rock wall as the fourth side. Fence posts are to be placed every \(12\) meters along the fence, including the two posts where the fence meets the rock wall. What is the fewest number of posts required to fence an area \(36\) m by \(60\) m?

[Figure 1](figures/1986_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Equal spacing suggests counting the \(12\)-meter gaps first. The three fenced sides form one continuous path, with a post at each end where it meets the wall.

[Figure 1](figures/1986_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

A side against the wall can have length \(60\) meters or \(36\) meters. Both fit along the \(100\)-meter wall.

With a \(60\)-meter side against the wall, the fenced sides have total length
\[
36+60+36=132\text{ meters}.
\]
This gives \(132\div12=11\) gaps. Starting with the first post, each gap leads to one additional post, so there are \(11+1=12\) posts.

With a \(36\)-meter side against the wall, the fence length is
\[
60+36+60=156\text{ meters},
\]
requiring \(156\div12+1=14\) posts. In both arrangements, the side lengths are multiples of \(12\), so the spacing places posts at the corners, and each shared corner is counted just once along the continuous path.

These are the only two side lengths that can lie along the wall. Therefore the fewest posts required is \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the two orientations and count gaps
